Thanks for the context, Marissa / Sam — quick technical reply with options and recommendations.

Short answer: Dedicated capacity is the most straightforward path to remove noisy-neighbor risk while keeping cost and time-to-value reasonable. Private VPC gives the strongest isolation but has more onboarding overhead.

Options:
1) Hosted Shared API (not recommended for your production SLOs)
   - Best for early experiments. Shared pool can exhibit latency variance under bursty workloads. We can do prefix caching and batching but cannot fully guarantee isolation.
2) Dedicated capacity (recommended trial -> production)
   - Dedicated GPU pools reserved for FinTechCo; isolation at the pool level prevents noisy neighbors from other tenants.
   - For ~200 rps and target 150ms P95 we recommend starting with: 8 x A10G-equivalent workers (continuous batching + KV cache) with headroom for bursts. This sizing assumes ~1-2k token average per request; we can refine after sample traces.
   - Benefits: low onboarding time (hours), bounded cost (monthly reserved), quick path to SLA-backed commitments at higher tiers.
3) Private VPC / On-prem (highest isolation)
   - Strongest network and tenancy isolation; recommended if you have regulatory constraints. Involves additional setup (VPC peering, customer-managed KMS, longer onboarding ~2-6 weeks).

Noisy-neighbor mitigations we provide:
- Pool-level isolation: dedicated pools do not share GPU hosts with other customers.
- Request prioritization & QoS: ability to rate-limit and prioritize traffic per-route.
- Autoscaling & headroom: autoscaling rules with buffer to prevent saturation-induced latency spikes.
- Continuous KV cache and prefix caching to lower token latency variance.
- Tracing & per-request metrics: per-route P95/P99 dashboards, token-level cost, and latency histograms.

Suggested SLO / Trial commitments:
- Trial: we can provision a small Dedicated pool (8 A10G-equivalent) for 2 weeks. During the trial we will instrument P50/P95/P99 and error rates and run a traffic mirror or partial production traffic (you suggested % routing). No SLA for trial but we will provide detailed metrics.
- Production Dedicated: we can commit to a contractual SLA at 99.9% monthly uptime for model serving on Dedicated (subject to agreed traffic patterns/concurrency limits). Network-level uptime depends on VPC/peering choices.

Operational asks from FinTechCo (to meet SLOs):
- Provide expected traffic shape (rps over time) and typical token counts per request.
- Agree on congestion behavior (e.g., how to handle bursts: queue vs reject) and acceptable retry behavior.
